title: YouCoded theme — the picture behind everything

steps.path: The picture behind the chat and panels: YouCoded on top, YouCoded Night underneath
steps.headline: Which picture should the YouCoded themes use? Each shows the light version above the night one.

variants.label: Glow
variants.summary: Large soft glows of lavender, violet and pink blending into each other, like setup's background but richer.
variants.risk: The calmest; may read as plain once panels cover most of it.

variants.label: Silk
variants.summary: Long flowing ribbons of violet and pink with a faint sheen, crossing the picture.

variants.label: Drift
variants.summary: A soft violet sky with floating out-of-focus lights.
variants.risk: The busiest behind see-through panels; text sits over the lights.

steps.headline: These are drawn by the app's own code, so YouCoded owns them outright. Is an abstract picture right, or do you want an illustrated scene?
steps.today: Cotton Candy Sky's picture is an artist's illustration (a girl on a cliff under a big moon). We don't know who drew it, so it can't be the default theme's picture.
steps.problem: Abstract pictures are safe and calm, but less charming than an illustrated scene.

options.label: Abstract, from above
pros: Calm behind text; works at any window size.
cons: No story or character in it.

options.label: An illustrated scene
options.summary: A purple scene made for YouCoded: commissioned from an illustrator, or generated with an image tool and checked for its licence.
pros: Charming and memorable, like Cotton Candy Sky.
cons: Takes longer and may cost money; a generated image's licence must allow shipping it in the app.
